what: Who is Natalie Harp, Trump's right-hand woman?

clean_source_blocks.text: One of Trump's longest serving and most loyal aides, Harp was thrust again into the spotlight when Democrat Jon Ossoff noted her closeness to the president.

Few people in US President Donald Trump's orbit have appeared as frequently by his side as Natalie Harp in recent years. One of Trump's longest-serving and most loyal aides, 35-year-old Harp is trusted with typing out his Truth Social posts, among other top responsibilities. She was thrust again into the spotlight this week by Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff - a Democrat and frequent Trump foil - when he recently name-checked her during a speech that has since gone viral. Ossoff attacked Trump's "travel with Natalie on their apparently defenceless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar", referring to the new Air Force One plane as well as to reports that Harp joined Trump - and a small group of people - when he secretly swapped planes leaving Turkey last month.

Six years later, Harp is now one of Trump’s closest and most devoted aides. Her official job title is special assistant to the president and executive assistant to the president on an annual salary of $150,000. Her unofficial job title is the “human printer” for supplying him with print-outs of information. And for years she has only been a minor character in the Trump Cinematic Universe. But all that changed this week when Jon Ossoff, a Democratic senator and possible 2028 presidential contender, accused Trump in a campaign speech of wanting to “build his ballroom and travel with Natalie” instead of doing his job.

Prominent Democrats and Republicans have spent the last three days fighting about Natalie Harp — a White House insider many Americans had never heard of until now. But why? A former host on the far-right One America News Network who has served as President Trump's executive assistant since he returned to office in 2025, Harp, 35, rocketed to the center of the national political conversation — and instantly became a trending topic online — after Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff briefly alluded to her while criticizing Trump during a campaign speech Sunday.

Few people in US President Donald Trump's orbit have appeared as frequently by his side as Natalie Harp in recent years.

One of Trump's longest-serving and most loyal aides, 35-year-old Harp is trusted with typing out his Truth Social posts, among other top responsibilities.

She was thrust again into the spotlight this week by Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff - a Democrat and frequent Trump foil - when he recently name-checked her during a speech that has since gone viral.

Ossoff attacked Trump's "travel with Natalie on their apparently defenceless flying palace gifted by the Emir of Qatar", referring to the new Air Force One plane as well as to reports that Harp joined Trump - and a small group of people - when he secretly swapped planes leaving Turkey last month.

Here is what you need to know about the Trump assistant who has been called both a "gatekeeper" and a "comfort blanket".

A California native and member of a conservative Christian family, Harp followed an unorthodox path into an already unconventional White House.

She rose to fame by crediting Trump with saving her life.

In his first term, Trump got the Right to Try Act passed to give some patients greater access to experimental treatments, which Harp used for her bone cancer. She quickly gained prominence and popularity in Trump's Maga (Make America Great Again) wing of the Republican party talking about the experience, and soon after joined an advisory board for Trump's 2020 re-election campaign.

"When I failed the chemotherapies that were on the market, no one wanted me in their clinical trials," she said at the 2020 Republican National Convention. "They didn't give me the right to try experimental treatments, Mr President. You did, and without you, I'd have died waiting for them to be approved."

After the event, Trump said: "She lit up the television screen like very few people I have ever seen do it."

Following Trump's loss in that election, Harp found work hosting a show at the conservative One Americans News Network, or OAN.

There, she became known as a ferocious Trump defender and prominent election denier. She left the network in 2022 to join Trump's next presidential campaign.

Most accounts of Trump's views of Harp come via anonymous second-hand sources in books by reporters such as Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan or Michael Wolff, and very little is publicly known about her private life.

Speculation about US president’s executive assistant sparks furious backlash from White House

Wearing shoulder-length blond hair, gold earrings and a red dress, cancer survivor Natalie Harp introduced herself to the 2020 Republican national convention as “a formerly forgotten American from California” and compared Donald Trump to George Bailey, the everyman hero played by James Stewart in the classic film It’s a Wonderful Life.

“George Bailey’s father was right,” smiled Harp, her voice echoing in the Andrew W Mellon auditorium in pandemic-hit Washington. “All you can take with you is that which you’ve given away. Mr President, that makes you the richest man in the world.”

Six years later, Harp is now one of Trump’s closest and most devoted aides. Her official job title is special assistant to the president and executive assistant to the president on an annual salary of $150,000.

Her unofficial job title is the “human printer” for supplying him with print-outs of information. And for years she has only been a minor character in the Trump Cinematic Universe.

But all that changed this week when Jon Ossoff, a Democratic senator and possible 2028 presidential contender, accused Trump in a campaign speech of wanting to “build his ballroom and travel with Natalie” instead of doing his job.

The remark triggered a tsunami of online speculation about the precise nature of the relationship and a furious backlash. On Monday Trump lashed out at the CNN reporter Kristen Holmes after she asked a question about Ossoff’s comments, while the White House’s anonymous “Rapid Response” team posted at Holmes: “Someday, your children will come across your disgusting and inhumane question.”

Far from dousing the flames, the White House had in fact poured kerosene on them, inadvertently enhancing Ossoff’s national standing among Democrats and inviting millions of people to ask the same question.

The 35-year-old Californian graduated from Point Loma Nazarene University, a Christian liberal arts college in San Diego, in 2012. Three years later, she earned an MBA from Liberty University, an evangelical college founded by Jerry Falwell in Lynchburg, Virginia.
